_about: Single source of truth for timing. animation.py (cameras, events, captions, titles) and tools/voiceover.py read this file. Times are seconds from the start of the video at 30 fps. 'text' is the caption/script text; 'tts' is what the voice engine reads (numbers spelled out).

scenes.name: EVERYONE IS A MILLIONAIRE
scenes.desc: A bright supermarket. The main customer (yellow hoodie) strides toward the checkout hugging a huge, wobbling pile of cash bundles, grinning; loose bills slip off the top. Other shoppers behind him also carry piles of cash. At the till the deadpan cashier turns round a little price card next to a single sandwich. Reverse angle: a snap zoom into the card: SANDWICH $1,999,999.99.
scenes.actions: Customer: proud strut, chin up, grin -> at the reveal his eyebrows shoot up, eyes widen, jaw drops. Cashier: half-lidded, bored, turns the card with one finger.
scenes.lighting: Cool fluorescent ceiling strips, warm window light from the street behind, light haze; slightly green "money" grade.
scenes.sfx: Upbeat plucked theme starts at once; cash rustle; a register beep; the price reveal lands on a comedic cash-register "ka-CHING" plus a falling-whistle; snap-zoom whoosh.

shots.name: hook_a
shots.camera: Tracking backwards in front of the customer at chest height, 35 mm, slight handheld bounce; he fills the lower-middle of the frame.

shots.name: hook_b
shots.camera: Over the cashier's shoulder onto the customer's face, 50 mm, slow push-in as his face falls.

shots.name: hook_c
shots.camera: Reverse angle over the customer's shoulder: fast snap zoom (eased) into the price card on the counter, 50 mm.

scenes.edit: Opens cold on motion (no fade). Hard cuts on the beats. Whip-smear into Scene 2.

scenes.name: THE FIRST MONEY TREE
scenes.desc: A quiet suburban street in golden morning light. Extreme close-up: a crisp banknote hangs from a twig among green leaves, sunbeams through the canopy. A hand reaches in and plucks it. Pull back: the same man (yellow hoodie) stands under an ordinary-looking tree whose branches are full of money; more bills flutter down and he jumps for joy. Wide: neighbours sprint across lawns, shake branches, scoop bills into bags and hold up phones.
scenes.actions: Main man: confused look at the bill -> big grin -> jumps with both arms up. Neighbours: run in, two shake branches, one crouches filling a bag, one takes a phone photo (flash).
scenes.lighting: Low warm sun from behind the tree; volumetric light shafts through the canopy; soft blue sky fill; dust and drifting bills catch the light.
scenes.sfx: Birdsong and a lawn sprinkler; leaves rustle; a soft paper "snap" as the bill is plucked; bills fluttering; running footsteps; crowd whoops; branch shakes; phone camera shutter.

shots.name: bill
shots.camera: Macro close-up of the banknote on the twig, 85 mm, shallow depth of field; slow drift in; a hand enters frame and plucks it.

shots.name: tree
shots.camera: Pull back and up from the man to reveal the whole tree, 28 mm.

shots.name: crowd
shots.camera: Wide, slow crane up and sideways as the neighbours swarm the tree, 24 mm.

scenes.edit: Whip-smear in from Scene 1. Title WHAT IF MONEY GREW ON TREES? at the top. Dip through a quick flash into Scene 3.

scenes.name: THE WORLD GOES CRAZY
scenes.desc: A farmer in a straw hat stands between his cornfield and one small money tree. He looks at the corn... looks at the money tree... and yanks up a corn stalk and throws it away. A man in a backyard kneels beside a potted sapling holding exactly ONE banknote, with a hand-made sign MY FIRST MONEY TREE, and presents it like a trophy. Aerial: endless rows of money trees and plastic greenhouses where corn used to be; a worker with a leaf blower blasts a river of bills onto a heap; sign MONEY FARM - EST. TODAY. Golden hour: a businessman in a suit stands on a hill with his arms spread before a forest of money trees that reaches the horizon; a SOLD sign beside him.
scenes.actions: Farmer: slow double-take, decision, yank and throw. Backyard dad: kneels, beams, "ta-da" hands. Worker: sweeps the leaf blower. Businessman: smug, arms spread wide.
scenes.lighting: Warm late-afternoon sun with long shadows; dust in the air over the farm; golden backlight and haze over the forest.
scenes.sfx: The music speeds up and adds layers (claps, whistle, shaker). Corn stalk rip and a whoosh; a tiny "ding" for the one-bill tree; leaf-blower drone and a gush of fluttering paper; a choir-like swell as the forest is revealed.

shots.name: farmer
shots.camera: Medium shot at the edge of the field, 35 mm, slow lateral track as he turns from the corn to the money tree.

shots.name: backyard
shots.camera: Low push-in on the proud owner and his one-bill sapling, 40 mm.

shots.name: farm
shots.camera: Drone glide over the money orchard and greenhouses, descending toward the leaf-blower worker, 24 mm.

shots.name: forest
shots.camera: Starts on the businessman's smug face and cranes up and back to reveal the forest to the horizon, 28 mm.

scenes.edit: Fast cuts on the beat; each shot is bigger and sillier than the last. Hard cut with a record scratch into Scene 4.

scenes.name: PRICES GO INSANE
scenes.desc: The supermarket again: shoppers push carts heaped with cash down the aisle; everything looks normal under a LOW PRICES EVERY DAY banner. Then a store owner in an apron walks the bread aisle with a price gun, flipping tags: $5 becomes $500. A woman at the dairy fridge watches the milk tag flip to $250 and her jaw drops. A shiny bicycle on display gets a giant $20,000 tag.
scenes.actions: Owner: brisk, cheerful, slaps on new tags. Woman shopper: double-take, jaw drop. Customers: stare at the bicycle tag.
scenes.lighting: Same fluorescent store, slightly harsher and greener as prices climb; product highlights.
scenes.sfx: Record scratch kills the music at the cut; a moment of muzak; then tense "documentary" pizzicato. Each tag flip: a price-gun click plus a register "ka-ching" pitched higher each time; a shocked gasp; cash rustle; cart squeak.

shots.name: store
shots.camera: Slow dolly down the main aisle at cart height, 28 mm.

shots.name: tags
shots.camera: Lateral track along the bread shelf as the owner re-tags it, ending on the $500 tag, 45 mm.

shots.name: milk
shots.camera: Push-in on the shocked shopper beside the milk tag, 40 mm.

shots.name: bike
shots.camera: Low arc around the bicycle and its huge tag, 30 mm.

scenes.edit: Fast cuts. Prices also pop up as big amber numbers at the top of the frame, marked as illustrative.

scenes.name: THE ECONOMY COLLAPSES
scenes.desc: A cashier is buried behind a mountain of cash while a counting machine sprays bills. A city street: money blows down the avenue like autumn leaves and everyone carries sacks of cash, while a huge screen on a building plots two lines: MONEY shoots straight up, GOODS barely moves. A shopper with two carts of cash takes the very last egg carton from an almost empty shelf (LIMIT 1 PER CUSTOMER).
scenes.actions: Cashier: frantic counting, sweating, deadpan. City crowd: walking with sacks, bills swirling round them. Shopper: reaches for the last eggs.
scenes.lighting: Overcast city with a low sun breaking through haze and side-lighting the bills; the screen glows; back in the store the light is colder.
scenes.sfx: Cash-counting machine whirr; city traffic and wind, paper blizzard; a low drum pulse and rising strings (dramatic, with a comic tuba-like bass); a downward "bwomp" as the dollar buys less.

shots.name: count
shots.camera: Push-in toward the cashier behind the cash mountain, 35 mm.

shots.name: city
shots.camera: Low wide dolly forward through the street among the people, tilting up toward the giant screen, 24 mm.

shots.name: graph
shots.camera: Looking up at the screen as the lines draw, slow push-in, 32 mm.

shots.name: struggle
shots.camera: Side track past the shopper to the nearly empty egg shelf, 35 mm.

scenes.edit: Hard cuts. The graph is labelled ILLUSTRATIVE.

scenes.name: THE FINAL TWIST
scenes.desc: Back to the first tree, now enormous and completely covered in banknotes. The man in the yellow hoodie shovels bills into a wheelbarrow. Then the same supermarket and the same checkout: he wheels the overflowing barrow up to the deadpan cashier, who turns the same price card: the old $1,999,999.99 is crossed out and the new price is $9,999,999.99. He turns and looks straight into the camera. Snap zoom into the price card, framed exactly like the opening.
scenes.actions: Man: determined shovelling -> proud push of the barrow -> face falls -> slow, deadpan look straight at the camera. Cashier: same bored card turn.
scenes.lighting: Giant tree: golden, backlit, volumetric shafts. Store: the exact lighting of Scene 1.
scenes.sfx: The playful theme returns, bigger; shovel scrapes and paper; wheelbarrow squeak; the card turn hits a ka-ching; silence for the stare; a final brass sting on "now it does", then a tiny "ding" on the price card.

shots.name: giant
shots.camera: Low angle on the man and the wheelbarrow, craning up to the giant money tree, 24 mm.

shots.name: final
shots.camera: Tracking beside the wheelbarrow to the checkout, 35 mm (matches the opening).

shots.name: stare
shots.camera: Over the cashier's shoulder: he turns his head and looks into the lens, 50 mm (matches hook_b).

shots.name: tagend
shots.camera: The opening's snap zoom into the price card, recreated; hold on the card.

scenes.edit: The ending re-creates the opening framing so the Short loops seamlessly back to the first frame.

lines.text: By noon, everyone on Earth was a millionaire. By dinner, nobody could afford a sandwich.
lines.tts: By noon, everyone on Earth was a millionaire. By dinner, nobody could afford a sandwich.

lines.text: It started when dollar bills began growing on trees.
lines.tts: It started when dollar bills began growing on trees.

lines.text: Within an hour, whole neighborhoods were out shaking branches.
lines.tts: Within an hour, whole neighborhoods were out shaking branches.

lines.text: Farmers ripped out their crops to plant money.
lines.tts: Farmers ripped out their crops to plant money.

lines.text: Families grew cash in their backyards.
lines.tts: Families grew cash in their backyards.

lines.text: And one man bought an entire forest, just to become the richest person alive.
lines.tts: And one man bought an entire forest, just to become the richest person alive.

lines.text: But then, something strange happened. Shops started raising their prices.
lines.tts: But then, something strange happened. Shops started raising their prices.

lines.text: A loaf of bread? $500. Milk? $250. A bicycle? $20,000.
lines.tts: A loaf of bread? Five hundred dollars. Milk? Two hundred and fifty. A bicycle? Twenty thousand.

lines.text: Here's the problem. Everyone had more money, but the world wasn't making any more food, houses or cars.
lines.tts: Here's the problem. Everyone had more money, but the world wasn't making any more food, houses or cars.

lines.text: Too much money, chasing too few goods. So every dollar bought less and less.
lines.tts: Too much money, chasing too few goods. So every dollar bought less and less.

lines.text: Soon, people needed a wheelbarrow of cash just to buy groceries.
lines.tts: Soon, people needed a wheelbarrow of cash just to buy groceries.

lines.text: Turns out, money really doesn't grow on trees.
lines.tts: Turns out, money really doesn't grow on trees.
